description: This line plot illustrates the normalized average gate value across different numbers of experts for seven distinct task categories—Intent, Summary, Law, Translation, Math, Code—and a Uniform baseline, as part of an evaluation in sparse architectural large language models. The x-axis, labeled “Experts,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 64, with major tick marks at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. The y-axis, labeled “Normalized Average Gate Value,” is linear and spans from 0.00 to 0.20, with tick marks at 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20. The “Intent” line (solid orange) starts near 0.08 at 1 expert and gradually declines to approximately 0.01 at 64 experts. The “Summary” line (solid blue) begins around 0.08 and decreases to about 0.01. The “Law” line (solid yellow) starts near 0.07 and falls to roughly 0.01. The “Translation” line (solid purple) begins at approximately 0.17 and steeply drops to about 0.01. The “Math” line (solid gray) starts near 0.06 and declines to around 0.01. The “Code” line (solid green) begins at approximately 0.07 and decreases to about 0.01. The “Uniform” line (dashed black) remains nearly flat across all expert counts, hovering consistently around 0.015. Shaded regions around each solid line represent uncertainty or variance, with the “Translation” category exhibiting the widest shaded area, particularly at lower expert counts.
